{{short description|Predicted physical phenomenon}}

[[File:MemoryIllustration.gif|right|thumb|As the gravitational wave propagates [[perpendicular]] to the plane of inertial masses (in [[free fall]]), it is displaced by an amount proportional to the gravitational wave strain. After the gravitational wave has passed, the masses are permanently displaced, due to the gravitational memory effect.]]

'''Gravitational memory effects''', also known as '''gravitational-wave memory effects''', are predicted persistent changes in the relative position of pairs of masses in space due to the passing of a [[gravitational wave]] (GW). Detection of gravitational memory effects has been suggested as a way of validating [[general relativity]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sutter |first=Paul M. |title=Could Gravitational-Wave ‘Memories’ Prove Einstein Wrong? |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/could-gravitational-wave-memories-prove-einstein-wrong/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref>

A linear approximation of [[Einstein field equations|Einstein's equations]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zel'dovich |first=Ya B. |last2=Polnarev |first2=A. G. |date=1974 |title=Radiation of gravitational waves by a cluster of superdense stars |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1974SvA....18...17Z/abstract |journal=Soviet Astronomy |language=en |volume=18 |pages=17 |issn=0038-5301}}</ref> was first proposed in 1974 by the Soviet scientists [[Yakov Zeldovich]] and [[A. G. Polnarev]];<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Beall |first=Abigail |date=August 2, 2023 |title=Does space-time remember? The search for gravitational memory |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg25934501-400-does-space-time-remember-the-search-for-gravitational-memory/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McCormick |first=Katie |date=December 8, 2021 |title=Gravitational Waves Should Permanently Distort Space-Time |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/gravitational-waves-should-permanently-distort-space-time-20211208/ |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> [[V. B. Braginsky|Vladimir Braginsky]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gorodetsky |first=Michael L. |last2=Levin |first2=Yuri |last3=Pinto |first3=Innocenzo M. |last4=Vyatchanin |first4=Sergei P. |date=2018 |title=Editorial – In Memoriam Vladimir Borisovich Braginsky |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0375960118305553 |journal=Physics Letters A |language=en |volume=382 |issue=33 |pages=2157–2164 |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2018.05.025|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[L. P. Grishchuk]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Braginsky |first=Vladimir B |last2=Kardashev |first2=Nikolai S |last3=Komberg |first3=Boris V |last4=Kurt |first4=Vladimir G |last5=Novikov |first5=Igor D |last6=Polnarev |first6=A G |last7=Postnov |first7=Konstantin A |last8=Rubakov |first8=Valerii A |last9=Rudenko |first9=Valentin N |last10=Thorne |first10=Kip S |last11=Cherepashchuk |first11=Anatolii M |last12=Shakura |first12=N I |date=2012-11-30 |title=In memory of Leonid Petrovich Grishchuk |url=https://ufn.ru/en/articles/2012/11/m/ |journal=Physics-Uspekhi |volume=55 |issue=11 |pages=1163–1165 |doi=10.3367/UFNe.0182.201211n.1247 |issn=1063-7869|url-access=subscription }}</ref> subsequently called these memory effects in 1985.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Braginskii |first=V. B. |last2=Grishchuk |first2=L. P. |date=1985 |title=Kinematic resonance and the memory effect in free mass gravitational antennas |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1985ZhETF..89..744B/abstract |journal=Zhurnal Eksperimentalnoi i Teoreticheskoi Fiziki |language=en |volume=89 |pages=744–750 |issn=0044-4510}}</ref> The '''non-linear memory effect''' was first proposed in the 1990s by [[Demetrios Christodoulou]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Christodoulou |first=Demetrios |date=1991-09-16 |title=Nonlinear nature of gravitation and gravitational-wave experiments |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.1486 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=67 |issue=12 |pages=1486–1489 |bibcode=1991PhRvL..67.1486C |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.1486 |issn=0031-9007 |pmid=10044168 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2014 [[Andrew Strominger]] and Alexander Zhiboedov showed that the formula related to the memory effect is the [[Fourier transform]] in time of [[Steven Weinberg]]'s [[soft graviton theorem]].<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=1411.5745 |class=hep-th |first1=Andrew |last1=Strominger |first2=Alexander |last2=Zhiboedov |title=Gravitational Memory, BMS Supertranslations and Soft Theorems |date=2014}}</ref> In general, memory effects are related to asymptotic behavior of the gravitational fields, as expected in [[Bondi–Metzner–Sachs group]] through the infrared triangle.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Strominger |first=Andrew |title=Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory |date=2018 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-17973-5 |location=Princeton}}</ref> At [[null infinity]], passing GWs leave a permanent distortion in [[spacetime]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Choi |first=Charles |date=2016-10-12 |title=Gravitational Waves May Permanently Alter Spacetime |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/article/gravitational-wave-memory/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=www.pbs.org |language=en-US}}</ref> changing distances between objects and shifting observers. Observers who initially agree on the origin of their coordinate system may not agree after the waves pass. This leads to ambiguities, or supertranslations, in defining the [[angular momentum]] carried by GWs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nadis |first=Steve |date=2022-07-13 |title=Mass and Angular Momentum, Left Ambiguous by Einstein, Get Defined |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mass-and-angular-momentum-left-ambiguous-by-einstein-get-defined-20220713/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

'''Gravitational spin memory''' is a proposed memory effect caused by GWs carrying [[angular momentum]] leave a gravitational memory effect in the travel times of light sent around a closed loop in opposite directions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCormick |first=Katie |date=December 8, 2021 |title=Gravitational Waves Should Permanently Distort Space-Time |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/gravitational-waves-should-permanently-distort-space-time-20211208/ |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite AV media |url=https://video.thinktv.org/video/can-the-universe-remember-exploring-gravitational-memory-dsugjo/ |title=Can Space Time Remember? |date=November 14, 2024 |last=Pollack |first=Christopher |last2=O'Dowd |first2=Matt |type=Video |publisher=PBS |series=[[PBS Space Time|Space Time]]}}</ref> This proposed memory effect was published by Strominger, Zhiboedov, and one of Strominger's graduate students, [[Sabrina Pasterski]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pasterski |first1=Sabrina |last2=Strominger |first2=Andrew |last3=Zhiboedov |first3=Alexander |date=14 December 2016 |title=New gravitational memories |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2016 |issue=12 |page=53 |arxiv=1502.06120 |bibcode=2016JHEP...12..053P |doi=10.1007/JHEP12(2016)053 |s2cid=256045385}}</ref>

Memory effects are weaker than the oscillatory signals detected with [[Ground-based interferometric gravitational-wave search|ground-based interferometers]] such as [[LIGO]]. Proposed approaches include stacking many events statistically and using low frequency space-based detectors such as [[Laser Interferometer Space Antenna|LISA]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> [[Core-collapse supernovae]] may generate strong memory effects because the explosions can be asymmetric. Such signals could be detected with proposed lunar-based detectors. Ramp-up signals may also be detectable on Earth with [[seismic noise]] filtering from relatively close supernovae, like those within the [[Milky Way]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-01-20 |title=Wrinkles in space–time could remember the secrets of exploding stars |url=https://physicsworld.com/wrinkles-in-spacetime-could-remember-the-secrets-of-exploding-stars/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>
